 1 dead in Henderson after heavy rain triggers three water rescue operations
 The National Weather Service issued a flood advisory in the southeast Las Vegas Valley as rainfall hit 0.50 inches in a 30-minute span just after noon.
 A bus passes a car which is stalled in floodwaters that cover McLeod Drive just north of Desert Inn Road Friday, October 30, 2026. (Sam Morris/Las Vegas Review-Journal) A woman is rescued from car stalled in floodwaters that cover McLeod Drive just north of Desert Inn Road Friday, October 30, 2026. (Sam Morris/Las Vegas Review-Journal) Vehicles travel through floodwaters that cover McLeod Drive just north of Desert Inn Road Friday, October 30, 2026. (Glenn Puit/Las Vegas Review-Journal) More Stories Rain on Halloween? 38-year dry streak likely to end — but Las Vegas trick-or-treaters shouldn’t fret More October storms dump rain on parts of Las Vegas area — PHOTOS Golf ball-sized hail pound parts of Arizona — PHOTOS More October showers coming to Las Vegas Valley 
 By Trevor Squire and Glenn Puit 
 / 
 Las Vegas Review-Journal 
 October 30, 2026 - 12:42 pm 
 Updated October 30, 2026 - 5:54 pm 
 A person who was rescued from a wash by Henderson firefighters on Friday near Lake Mead Parkway went into cardiac arrest and died, a Henderson city spokesperson said.
 “Upon rescue, the subject went into cardiac arrest and crews provided immediate care,” the spokesperson said in an email Friday afternoon. “The subject was transported to a local hospital and was pronounced deceased.”
 The rescue was one of three such swift-water operations carried out by the Henderson Fire Department early Friday afternoon as rain deluged parts of the city and the Las Vegas Valley.
 Two people were also rescued near Lake Mead Parkway east of the Lake Las Vegas entrance and another person was rescued from the top of a vehicle near North Milan Street and Drake Street in Henderson. There were no injuries reported.
 Meanwhile, as rain and hail battered parts of the valley, flooding some streets, Tim Davis of Las Vegas was headed to a doctor’s appointment, riding his motorcycle, when the skies unloaded as he approached the on-ramp to Interstate 11 at Charleston Boulevard.
 “As we were getting on the onramp we hit massive hail,” Davis said. “We had to pull off.
 Davis said he wasn’t wearing a full motorcycle helmet and he got pelted.
 “I got nailed in the groin with a piece of hail about yay big,” Davis said, holding his fingers up to form a small circle.
 Davis was among many motorists in Las Vegas who were hit with waves of showers, thunderstorms and even hail Friday.
 The National Weather Service Las Vegas office issued a flash flood warning until 3:45 p.m. across eastern Henderson and Lake Las Vegas, where rainfall hit 0.50 inches in a 30-minute span just after noon. According to county rain gauge data, several parts of eastern Henderson had one to over 1.5 inches of rain.
 Heavy rain was also falling in downtown Las Vegas, which saw just over an inch of rain through Friday afternoon, according to county rain gauge data. Ping pong ball-sized hail was also reported east of downtown Las Vegas, according to an X post by the NWS.
 “We are keeping an eye on it,” Chris Outler, a meteorologist with the NWS, said. “If it keeps raining hard enough we could see some greater impacts. We are going to have to wait and see how things unfold.”
 Outler said the public should “stay alert and if you do encounter flood waters turn around.”
 🚨 Heads up! The flood advisory has been upgraded to a Flash Flood Warning for the Cadence and old Henderson areas! Over 1 inch of rain has fallen in parts of the area since noon. #nvwx https://t.co/4mlXZkz3Be
 — NWS Las Vegas (@NWSVegas) October 30, 2026 
 A previous flood advisory listed hazards of heavy rain, nuisance flooding and wind gusts of over 40 mph.
 “Be mindful of flowing washes in the area and flooded low water crossings,” the NWS said in a post on X.
 Contact Trevor Squire at tsquire@reviewjournal.com. Follow him at @trevordsquire on X. Contact Glenn Puit at gpuit@reviewjournal.com .
